newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. senators leave Seoul for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators leave Seoul for North Korea.

text.p: Five U.S. senators headed to Pyongyang on Friday after a three-day trip to South Korea where North Korea topped their agenda, Seoul officials said.

They were the most prominent U.S. travellers to the communist state since last November when Bill Richardson, then a New Mexico congressman, was sent to free a U.S. citizen who had sneaked into the North and was accused of spying.
Richardson is now the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations.
Seoul and Washington have invited North Korea to attend four-party peace talks, along with China.
At a meeting in New York on Wednesday, Pyongyang asked the United States and South Korea to guarantee food aid as a condition for accepting.
A South Korean official on Friday called the request "ridiculous".
The delegation led by Ted Stevens, the chairman of the Senate Appropriations Committee, met South Korean President Kim Young-sam and toured the Demilitarized Zone dividing the Korean peninsula.
Members did not meet the media or divulge any details of their visit to North Korea.

Michael Breen, a North Korea watcher in Seoul, said: "The Republican senators might want to assess the threat by North Korea on the peninsula as they are uneasy about Clinton's policy towards the North".
Accompanying Stevens are Republicans Pete Domenici of New Mexico, Thad Cochran of Mississippi, Pat Roberts of Kansas and Democrat Daniel Inouye of Hawaii.
The senators flew to Pyongyang from Seoul via a third country's airspace.
